critical_code_review_comments: server.py::continuity_sentinel — good defensive JSON parsing (strips ```json fences, silently ignores parse errors returning flags=[]). Consider surfacing parse failures via a debug field so main agent can diagnose LLM regressions rather than silently returning empty flags.

Sidebar.jsx PageGroup component — the file is now ~1217 lines. Once past ~700 lines the review guidelines recommend splitting; PageGroup + ChapterRow could be extracted into their own module for readability.

delete_chapter endpoint uses two sequential Mongo writes (update_many pages, then delete_one chapter). Not atomic — a crash between them leaves orphan pages with a stale chapter_id. Consider a session/transaction or reverse ordering (delete chapter first, then unfile pages) so failures leave a recoverable state.

Frontend moveSceneToChapter → PATCH /api/pages accepts chapter_id but there is no server-side validation that the chapter belongs to the same project/user. Sending another user's chapter_id (or a chapter from a different project) will be silently persisted. Not exploitable across users due to user_id filter on chapters listing, but cross-project moves are possible — recommend validating chapter_id ownership + project match in update_page.
